From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Hi Sam / Priya —

Thanks — below are our point-by-point responses for the hosted API. I've kept answers concise for your binder; happy to expand any item. Attached: redwood-data-lifecycle-diagram.png (high-level flow showing primary region, backups, caches, and deletion flows).

1) Data residency / region choice- We support customer selection of a primary region at account activation. For Arkwright you can pin the account to a single US region (us-west-2 or us-east-1). Primary customer payloads and derived artifacts (embeddings if generated by request) are stored in that selected region by default.

2) Default retention windows- Customer request/response payloads: default ephemeral storage is 30 days for hosted API accounts unless a longer custom retention is requested and contractually approved.- Audit logs and routing metadata: 90 days by default.- Backups/snapshots (for disaster recovery): retained for 90 calendar days.

3) Backups, snapshots, and residual copies- Backups are taken in-region and encrypted; they are retained for 90 days. We do not replicate backup content to other regions unless a customer contract explicitly requests geo-redundant backups.- Short-lived caches (KV cache, inference caches) are in-memory or in local cache layers and are purged on session expiry; they are not written to long-term object storage.

4) Deletion / erasure SLA and process- Customer-initiated erasure: when Arkwright requests a full account data erasure (via the Console or signed request), we begin a multi-step purge: a) remove accessible objects from primary stores (completed within 24–72 hours depending on size), b) remove entries from service indexes and search within 3–5 business days, and c) delete backups/snapshots within 7–30 days depending on backup cycle and retention window. The full completion (including backup expiry) is typically within 30 days; we commit to process backups for accelerated deletion within 7 business days when requested under contract.- Legal holds or regulatory obligations will suspend deletion until released; we will notify the customer if a hold applies.

5) Derivative artifacts (embeddings, fine‑tune caches)- Derivatives created explicitly for your account (e.g., embeddings generated from your inputs) are stored in the primary region and are scoped to your account. They follow the same retention and deletion timelines as other customer data. If you request deletion of the source data and derivatives, we will delete both according to the erasure SLA above.

6) Logs, monitoring, and telemetry- Operational logs (used for debugging and SRE): 90 days by default.- Audit logs and access traces required for compliance can be exported to customer-managed storage on request (we provide S3-compatible exports).

7) Encryption & key management- All customer data at rest is encrypted with AES‑256. Keys are managed in our KMS; for Private/Dedicated customers we offer customer-managed keys (CMK) integration. For hosted customers like Arkwright we can also support a dedicated KMS integration as part of an enterprise addendum.

8) Cache / in-memory concerns- The serving runtime uses in-memory KV caches and transient GPU memory for model state; these are ephemeral per request/tenant and are not persisted to object storage. On a deletion request we zero sensitive caches and rotate in-memory contexts per best practices.

9) Evidence and attestation- We can provide: (a) an export of the deletion event and job id when a purge is executed, (b) an excerpt of audit logs showing the deletion workflow, and (c) a standard attestation letter describing our processes (we can produce a signed attestation for Arkwright's vendor binder).

10) Certifications & controls- Redwood Inference maintains SOC 2 Type II and publishes an inventory of controls. We also provide a security questionnaire pack on request with control mappings.

If you prefer tighter windows (e.g., 7‑day backup expiry, shorter log retention), we can include those in a contractual addendum.

Attachments: redwood-data-lifecycle-diagram.png

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Product Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

Kimberly / Ben —

Thanks — this is exactly what we needed and clear to our compliance reviewers. A couple of small clarifications before we close the binder:

• When you say "short-lived caches are purged on session expiry" — can you confirm there are no disk-backed swap snapshots or paging files that could contain plaintext copies beyond memory?
• For embeddings: will deleting the source text guarantee downstream models and index shards no longer contain recoverable slices of the original? We need wording we can put in the vendor contract.

If you can send the attestation letter and a one‑paragraph confirmation on cache/paging behavior, we can complete vendor approval this week.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

—Sam
Information Security, Arkwright Financial
